ID: [Performance] Do not use floating point data types
Name: AVOID_FLOATING_POINT_DATA_TYPES
Description: The "Double" floating point data type should be avoided, as it can result in unpredictable roundoff errors and decreased performance in certain scenarios. Use "Int64" or "Decimal" where appropriate (but note that "Decimal" is limited to 4 digits after the decimal sign).

ID: [Performance] Set IsAvailableInMdx to false on non-attribute columns
Name: ISAVAILABLEINMDX_FALSE_NONATTRIBUTE_COLUMNS
Description:
To speed up processing time and conserve memory after processing, attribute hierarchies should not be built for columns that are never used for slicing by MDX clients. In other words, all hidden columns that are not used as a Sort By Column or referenced in user hierarchies should have their IsAvailableInMdx property set to false.
Reference: https://blog.crossjoin.co.uk/2018/07/02/isavailableinmdx-ssas-tabular/
Expression:
IsAvailableInMDX
and

(IsHidden or Table.IsHidden)
and

not UsedInSortBy.Any() 
and

not UsedInHierarchies.Any()
and
not UsedInVariations.Any()
and
SortByColumn = null

ID: [Performance] Avoid bi-directional relationships against high-cardinality columns
Name: AVOID_BI-DIRECTIONAL_RELATIONSHIPS_AGAINST_HIGH-CARDINALITY_COLUMNS
Description: For best performance, it is recommended to avoid using bi-directional relationships against high-cardinality columns. In order to run this rule, you must first run the script shown here: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/vertipaqintabulareditor

ID: [Performance] Reduce usage of long-length columns with high cardinality
Name: REDUCE_USAGE_OF_LONG-LENGTH_COLUMNS_WITH_HIGH_CARDINALITY
Description: It is best to avoid lengthy text columns. This is especially true if the column has many unique values. These types of columns can cause longer processing times, bloated model sizes, as well as slower user queries. Long length is defined as more than 100 characters.

ID: [Performance] Split date and time
Name: SPLIT_DATE_AND_TIME
Description:
This rule finds datetime columns that have values not at midnight. To maximize performance, the time element should be split from date element (or the time component should be rounded to midnight as this will reduce column cardinality).
Reference: https://www.sqlbi.com/articles/separate-date-and-time-in-powerpivot-and-bism-tabular/

ID: [Performance] Large tables should be partitioned
Name: LARGE_TABLES_SHOULD_BE_PARTITIONED
Description: Large tables should be partitioned in order to optimize processing. In order for this rule to run properly, you must run the script shown here: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/vertipaqintabulareditor

ID: [Performance] Reduce usage of calculated columns that use the RELATED function
Name: REDUCE_USAGE_OF_CALCULATED_COLUMNS_THAT_USE_THE_RELATED_FUNCTION
Description:
Calculated columns do not compress as well as data columns and may cause longer processing times. As such, calculated columns should be avoided if possible. One scenario where they may be easier to avoid is if they use the RELATED function.
Reference: https://www.sqlbi.com/articles/storage-differences-between-calculated-columns-and-calculated-tables/

ID: [Performance] Consider a star-schema instead of a snowflake architecture
Name: SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA_ARCHITECTURE
Description:
Generally speaking, a star-schema is the optimal architecture for tabular models. That being the case, there are valid cases to use a snowflake approach. Please check your model and consider moving to a star-schema architecture.
Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/guidance/star-schema

ID: [Performance] Model should have a date table
Name: MODEL_SHOULD_HAVE_A_DATE_TABLE
Description: Generally speaking, models should generally have a date table. Models that do not have a date table generally are not taking advantage of features such as time intelligence or may not have a properly structured architecture.

ID: [Performance] Date/calendar tables should be marked as a date table
Name: DATE/CALENDAR_TABLES_SHOULD_BE_MARKED_AS_A_DATE_TABLE
Description:
This rule looks for tables that contain the words 'date' or 'calendar' as they should likely be marked as a date table.
Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-date-tables
Expression:
(Name.ToUpper().Contains("DATE") or Name.ToUpper().Contains("CALENDAR"))

and

(
DataCategory <> "Time"

or

Columns.Any(IsKey == true && DataType == "DateTime") == false
)

ID: [Performance] Remove auto-date table
Name: REMOVE_AUTO-DATE_TABLE
Description:
Avoid using auto-date tables. Make sure to turn off auto-date table in the settings in Power BI Desktop. This will save memory resources. 
Reference: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xu3uDEHtCrg
Expression:
ObjectTypeName == "Calculated Table"

and

(
Name.StartsWith("DateTableTemplate_") 

or 

Name.StartsWith("LocalDateTable_")
)

ID: [Performance] Avoid excessive bi-directional or many-to-many relationships
Name: AVOID_EXCESSIVE_BI-DIRECTIONAL_OR_MANY-TO-MANY_RELATIONSHIPS
Description:
Limit use of b-di and many-to-many relationships. This rule flags the model if more than 30% of relationships are bi-di or many-to-many.
Reference: https://www.sqlbi.com/articles/bidirectional-relationships-and-ambiguity-in-dax/

ID: [Performance] Limit row level security (RLS) logic
Name: LIMIT_ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY_(RLS)_LOGIC
Description: Try to simplify the DAX used for row level security. Usage of the functions within this rule can likely be offloaded to the upstream systems (data warehouse).

ID: [Performance] Consider using aggregations if using Direct Query in Power BI
Name: MODEL_USING_DIRECT_QUERY_AND_NO_AGGREGATIONS
Description:
If using Direct Query in Power BI Premium, you may want to consider using aggregations in order to boost performance.
Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-aggregations
Expression:
Tables.Any(ObjectTypeName == "Table (DirectQuery)")
and


AllColumns.Any(AlternateOf != null) == false
and 
DefaultPowerBIDataSourceVersion.ToString() == "PowerBI_V3"

ID: [Performance] Minimize Power Query transformations
Name: MINIMIZE_POWER_QUERY_TRANSFORMATIONS
Description:
Minimize Power Query transformations in order to improve model processing performance. It is a best practice to offload these transformations to the data warehouse if possible. Also, please check whether query folding is occurring within your model. Please reference the article below for more information on query folding.
Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-query/power-query-folding
Expression:
SourceType.ToString() = "M"
and
(
Query.Contains("Table.Combine(")
or

Query.Contains("Table.Join(")
or

Query.Contains("Table.NestedJoin(")
or
Query.Contains("Table.AddColumn(")
or
Query.Contains("Table.Group(")
or
Query.Contains("Table.Sort(")
or
Query.Contains("Table.Pivot(")
or
Query.Contains("Table.Unpivot(")
or
Query.Contains("Table.UnpivotOtherColumns(")
or
Query.Contains("Table.Distinct(")
or
Query.Contains("[Query=""SELECT")
or
Query.Contains("Value.NativeQuery")
or
Query.Contains("OleDb.Query")
or
Query.Contains("Odbc.Query")
)

ID: [Performance] Avoid using many-to-many relationships on tables used for dynamic row level security
Name: AVOID_USING_MANY-TO-MANY_RELATIONSHIPS_ON_TABLES_USED_FOR_DYNAMIC_ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY
Description:
Using many-to-many relationships on tables which use dynamic row level security can cause serious query performance degradation. This pattern's performance problems compound when snowflaking multiple many-to-many relationships against a table which contains row level security. Instead, use one of the patterns shown in the article below where a single dimension table relates many-to-one to a security table.

Reference: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/dynamicrlspatterns

ID: [Performance] Unpivot pivoted (month) data
Name: UNPIVOT_PIVOTED_(MONTH)_DATA
Description:
Avoid using pivoted data in your tables. This rule checks specifically for pivoted data by month.
Reference: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/top10bestpractices
Expression:
Columns.Any(Name.ToUpper().Contains("JAN") && (DataType == DataType.Int64 || DataType == DataType.Decimal || DataType == DataType.Double))
and
Columns.Any(Name.ToUpper().Contains("FEB") && (DataType == DataType.Int64 || DataType == DataType.Decimal || DataType == DataType.Double))
and
Columns.Any(Name.ToUpper().Contains("MAR") && (DataType == DataType.Int64 || DataType == DataType.Decimal || DataType == DataType.Double))
and
Columns.Any(Name.ToUpper().Contains("APR") && (DataType == DataType.Int64 || DataType == DataType.Decimal || DataType == DataType.Double))
and
Columns.Any(Name.ToUpper().Contains("MAY") && (DataType == DataType.Int64 || DataType == DataType.Decimal || DataType == DataType.Double))
and
Columns.Any(Name.ToUpper().Contains("JUN") && (DataType == DataType.Int64 || DataType == DataType.Decimal || DataType == DataType.Double))

ID: [Performance] Many-to-many relationships should be single-direction
Name: MANY-TO-MANY_RELATIONSHIPS_SHOULD_BE_SINGLE-DIRECTION

ID: [Performance] Reduce usage of calculated tables
Name: REDUCE_USAGE_OF_CALCULATED_TABLES
Description: Migrate calculated table logic to your data warehouse. Reliance on calculated tables will lead to technical debt and potential misalignments if you have multiple models on your platform.

ID: [Performance] Remove redundant columns in related tables
Name: REMOVE_REDUNDANT_COLUMNS_IN_RELATED_TABLES
Description: Removing unnecessary columns reduces model size and speeds up data loading.
Expression:
UsedInRelationships.Any() == false 
and
Model.AllColumns.Any(Name == current.Name and Table.Name != current.Table.Name and Table.UsedInRelationships.Any(FromTable.Name == current.Table.Name))

ID: [Performance] Measures using time intelligence and model is using Direct Query
Name: MEASURES_USING_TIME_INTELLIGENCE_AND_MODEL_IS_USING_DIRECT_QUERY
Description: At present, time intelligence functions are known to not perform as well when using Direct Query. If you are having performance issues, you may want to try alternative solutions such as adding columns in the fact table that show previous year or previous month data.
Expression:
Model.Tables.Any(ObjectTypeName == "Table (DirectQuery)")
and
(
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"CLOSINGBALANCEMONTH\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"CLOSINGBALANCEQUARTER\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"CLOSINGBALANCEYEAR\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"DATEADD\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"DATESBETWEEN\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"DATESINPERIOD\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"DATESMTD\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"DATESQTD\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"DATESYTD\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"ENDOFMONTH\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"ENDOFQUARTER\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"ENDOFYEAR\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"FIRSTDATE\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"FIRSTNONBLANK\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"FIRSTNONBLANKVALUE\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"LASTDATE\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"LASTNONBLANK\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"LASTNONBLANKVALUE\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"NEXTDAY\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"NEXTMONTH\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"NEXTQUARTER\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"NEXTYEAR\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"OPENINGBALANCEMONTH\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"OPENINGBALANCEQUARTER\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"OPENINGBALANCEYEAR\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"PARALLELPERIOD\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"PREVIOUSDAY\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"PREVIOUSMONTH\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"PREVIOUSQUARTER\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"PREVIOUSYEAR\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"STARTOFMONTH\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"STARTOFQUARTER\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"STARTOFYEAR\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"TOTALMTD\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"TOTALQTD\s*\(")
or
RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"TOTALYTD\s*\(")
)

ID: [Performance] Reduce number of calculated columns
Name: REDUCE_NUMBER_OF_CALCULATED_COLUMNS
Description:
Calculated columns do not compress as well as data columns so they take up more memory. They also slow down processing times for both the table as well as process recalc. Offload calculated column logic to your data warehouse and turn these calculated columns into data columns.
Reference: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/top10bestpractices

ID: [Performance] Check if bi-directional and many-to-many relationships are valid
Name: CHECK_IF_BI-DIRECTIONAL_AND_MANY-TO-MANY_RELATIONSHIPS_ARE_VALID
Description:
Bi-directional and many-to-many relationships may cause performance degradation or even have unintended consequences. Make sure to check these specific relationships to ensure they are working as designed and are actually necessary.
Reference: https://www.sqlbi.com/articles/bidirectional-relationships-and-ambiguity-in-dax/
Expression:
FromCardinality.ToString() = "Many" and ToCardinality.ToString() = "Many"
or
CrossFilteringBehavior == CrossFilteringBehavior.BothDirections

ID: [Performance] Check if dynamic row level security (RLS) is necessary
Name: CHECK_IF_DYNAMIC_ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY_(RLS)_IS_NECESSARY
Description:
Usage of dynamic row level security (RLS) can add memory and performance overhead. Please research the pros/cons of using it.
Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/admin/service-admin-rls

ID: [DAX Expressions] Column references should be fully qualified
Name: DAX_COLUMNS_FULLY_QUALIFIED
Description:
Using fully qualified column references makes it easier to distinguish between column and measure references, and also helps avoid certain errors. When referencing a column in DAX, first specify the table name, then specify the column name in square brackets.
Reference: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/top10bestpractices

ID: [DAX Expressions] Measure references should be unqualified
Name: DAX_MEASURES_UNQUALIFIED
Description:
Using unqualified measure references makes it easier to distinguish between column and measure references, and also helps avoid certain errors. When referencing a measure using DAX, do not specify the table name. Use only the measure name in square brackets.
Reference: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/top10bestpractices

ID: [DAX Expressions] No two measures should have the same definition
Name: AVOID_DUPLICATE_MEASURES
Description: Two measures with different names and defined by the same DAX expression should be avoided to reduce redundancy.

ID: [DAX Expressions] Use the TREATAS function instead of INTERSECT for virtual relationships
Name: USE_THE_TREATAS_FUNCTION_INSTEAD_OF_INTERSECT
Description:
The TREATAS function is more efficient and provides better performance than the INTERSECT function when used in virutal relationships.
Reference:  https://www.sqlbi.com/articles/propagate-filters-using-treatas-in-dax/

ID: [DAX Expressions] Use the DIVIDE function for division
Name: USE_THE_DIVIDE_FUNCTION_FOR_DIVISION
Description:
Use the DIVIDE  function instead of using "/". The DIVIDE function resolves divide-by-zero cases. As such, it is recommended to use to avoid errors.

Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/guidance/dax-divide-function-operator

ID: [DAX Expressions] Avoid using the IFERROR function
Name: AVOID_USING_THE_IFERROR_FUNCTION
Description:
Avoid using the IFERROR function as it may cause performance degradation. If you are concerned about a divide-by-zero error, use the DIVIDE function as it naturally resolves such errors as blank (or you can customize what should be shown in case of such an error).
Reference: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/top10bestpractices

ID: [DAX Expressions] Measures should not be direct references of other measures
Name: MEASURES_SHOULD_NOT_BE_DIRECT_REFERENCES_OF_OTHER_MEASURES
Description: This rule identifies measures which are simply a reference to another measure. As an example, consider a model with two measures: [MeasureA] and [MeasureB]. This rule would be triggered for MeasureB if MeasureB's DAX was MeasureB:=[MeasureA]. Such duplicative measures should be removed.

ID: [DAX Expressions] Store duplicate measure references in a variable
Name: DUPLICATE_MEASURE_REFERENCE_WITHOUT_VAR
Description: The same measure is referenced more than once in this expression. Even within the same filter context, the formula engine may evaluate the measure redundantly — once per reference. Store the result in a VAR before conditional logic and reference the variable instead: VAR _result = [Measure] RETURN IF(_result > 0, _result). Important: define the VAR only where it is guaranteed to be used — declaring it before a SWITCH or IF can be counterproductive if only one branch executes, as all variables are evaluated regardless of which branch runs. Reference: https://www.sqlbi.com/articles/optimizing-if-and-switch-expressions-using-variables/

ID: [DAX Expressions] Do not add columns directly in SUMMARIZE - use ADDCOLUMNS instead
Name: USE_ADDCOLUMNS_WITH_SUMMARIZE
Description: Using SUMMARIZE to add computed columns inline (e.g. SUMMARIZE(Table, [Col], "Name", Expression)) can produce incorrect results due to context transition issues. Always separate grouping from aggregation: ADDCOLUMNS(SUMMARIZE(Table, [Col]), "Name", CALCULATE(Expression)). Reference: https://www.sqlbi.com/articles/best-practices-using-summarize-and-addcolumns/

ID: [DAX Expressions] Use COALESCE instead of IF(ISBLANK([Measure]), 0, [Measure])
Name: USE_COALESCE_INSTEAD_OF_IF_ISBLANK
Description: The pattern IF(ISBLANK([Measure]), 0, [Measure]) or IF([Measure] = BLANK(), 0, [Measure]) evaluates the measure twice — once in the condition and once in the result branch — causing redundant formula engine evaluations. Replace with COALESCE([Measure], 0), which evaluates the measure only once and returns the first non-BLANK value. Reference: https://dax.guide/coalesce/

ID: [DAX Expressions] Use COUNTROWS instead of COUNT
Name: USE_COUNTROWS_INSTEAD_OF_COUNT
Description: COUNT(Table[Column]) counts non-BLANK values in a column, which means rows with BLANK are silently ignored and results can be incorrect. COUNTROWS(Table) counts all rows regardless of BLANK values in any column, is more efficient, and makes the intent of the formula self-evident. Replace COUNT(Table[Column]) with COUNTROWS(Table). Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dax/best-practices/dax-countrows

ID: [DAX Expressions] Filter column values with proper syntax
Name: FILTER_COLUMN_VALUES
Description:
Instead of using this pattern FILTER('Table','Table'[Column]="Value") for the filter parameters of a CALCULATE or CALCULATETABLE function, use one of the options below. As far as whether to use the KEEPFILTERS function, see the second reference link below.

Option 1: KEEPFILTERS('Table'[Column]="Value")
Option 2: 'Table'[Column]="Value"

Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/guidance/dax-avoid-avoid-filter-as-filter-argument
Reference: https://www.sqlbi.com/articles/using-keepfilters-in-dax/

ID: [Performance] Filter columns, not tables, in CALCULATE and CALCULATETABLE
Name: FILTER_COLUMNS_NOT_TABLES
Description: Using FILTER over an entire table (e.g. FILTER(Sales, condition) or FILTER(ALL(Sales), condition)) as a filter argument in CALCULATE or CALCULATETABLE filters the expanded table, which includes all related dimension columns. This causes incorrect results due to unintended cross-table intersections and severe performance degradation. Use column filters instead: CALCULATE([Measure], Sales[Amount] > 100) or KEEPFILTERS(Sales[Amount] > 100). Note: complements the Microsoft rule FILTER_COLUMN_VALUES. Reference: https://www.sqlbi.com/articles/filter-columns-not-tables-in-dax/

ID: [Performance] Avoid volatile functions in calculated columns and tables
Name: AVOID_VOLATILE_FUNCTIONS_IN_CALCULATED
Description: Volatile functions such as NOW(), TODAY(), RAND(), RANDBETWEEN(), UTCNOW(), and UTCTODAY() should not be used inside calculated columns or calculated tables. These functions are recalculated every time the model is opened in Power BI Desktop, significantly increasing load times. Use them only inside measures. Reference: https://www.sqlbi.com/blog/marco/2022/04/30/about-waiting-time-for-power-bi-desktop-to-open/

ID: [Performance] Avoid useless Power Query steps (Table.Sort and Table.ReorderColumns)
Name: AVOID_USELESS_POWER_QUERY_STEPS
Description: Table.Sort and Table.ReorderColumns are almost always useless in Power Query when loading data into a Tabular model. Table.Sort: Analysis Services does not guarantee or preserve row order — the engine reorders data during storage and query execution, so any sorting done in Power Query is discarded. Table.ReorderColumns: column order in the data model has no effect on reports or DAX calculations — Power BI ignores it entirely. Both steps consume CPU and memory during refresh with no benefit. Remove them unless there is a specific documented reason (e.g. Table.Sort feeding a Table.FirstN to retrieve top N rows).

ID: [Performance] Use SharePoint.Contents instead of SharePoint.Files
Name: USE_SHAREPOINT_CONTENTS_INSTEAD_OF_FILES
Description: SharePoint.Files retrieves metadata for every file in the SharePoint folder tree before filtering, which causes significant overhead. SharePoint.Contents loads only the folder structure and defers file enumeration, allowing query folding and lazy evaluation — this alone can yield up to 60% performance improvement on refresh. Replace SharePoint.Files(<url>) with SharePoint.Contents(<url>) and navigate to the target folder/files explicitly.

ID: [Performance] Avoid Table.ExpandTableColumn on SharePoint.Tables connections
Name: AVOID_EXPANDING_TABLE_COLUMNS_ON_SHAREPOINT_TABLES
Description: When connecting to SharePoint Lists via SharePoint.Tables, expanding Record-type columns using Table.ExpandTableColumn triggers additional HTTP requests per row to fetch the extra metadata — this causes severe performance degradation and may time out on large lists. Consider flattening the data at the source, using a different SharePoint connector, or limiting the columns expanded. Reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/optimize-expanding-table-columns

ID: [Performance] Use RelativePath and Query parameters in Web.Contents (Partition)
Name: WEB_CONTENTS_WITHOUT_RELATIVE_PATH_OR_QUERY
Description: Calling Web.Contents with a fully hardcoded URL (e.g. Web.Contents("https://api.example.com/data?param=value")) prevents query folding and blocks scheduled refresh in the Power BI Service, because the URL is treated as dynamic. Always split the base URL from dynamic parts using the optional record: Web.Contents("https://api.example.com", [RelativePath="data", Query=[param="value"]]). This allows Power BI to recognize the source as certified and enables refresh. Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/web-contents-function
Expression: SourceType.ToString() = "M" and Query.Contains("Web.Contents") and (not Query.Contains("RelativePath") or not Query.Contains("Query ="))

ID: [Performance] Use RelativePath and Query parameters in Web.Contents (Shared Expressions)
Name: WEB_CONTENTS_WITHOUT_RELATIVE_PATH_OR_QUERY_EXPRESSION
Description: Calling Web.Contents with a fully hardcoded URL (e.g. Web.Contents("https://api.example.com/data?param=value")) prevents query folding and blocks scheduled refresh in the Power BI Service, because the URL is treated as dynamic. Always split the base URL from dynamic parts using the optional record: Web.Contents("https://api.example.com", [RelativePath="data", Query=[param="value"]]). This allows Power BI to recognize the source as certified and enables refresh. Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/web-contents-function
Expression: Expression.Contains("Web.Contents") and (not Expression.Contains("RelativePath") or not Expression.Contains("Query ="))

ID: [DAX Expressions] Filter measure values by columns, not tables
Name: FILTER_MEASURE_VALUES_BY_COLUMNS
Description:
Instead of using this pattern FILTER('Table',[Measure]>Value) for the filter parameters of a CALCULATE or CALCULATETABLE function, use one of the options below (if possible). Filtering on a specific column will produce a smaller table for the engine to process, thereby enabling faster performance. Using the VALUES function or the ALL function depends on the desired measure result.

Option 1: FILTER(VALUES('Table'[Column]),[Measure] > Value)
Option 2: FILTER(ALL('Table'[Column]),[Measure] > Value)

Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/guidance/dax-avoid-avoid-filter-as-filter-argument

ID: [DAX Expressions] Inactive relationships that are never activated
Name: INACTIVE_RELATIONSHIPS_THAT_ARE_NEVER_ACTIVATED
Description:
Inactive relationships are activated using the USERELATIONSHIP function. If an inactive relationship is not referenced in any measure via this function, the relationship will not be used. It should be determined whether the relationship is not necessary or to activate the relationship via this method.

Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/guidance/relationships-active-inactive
Reference: https://dax.guide/userelationship/
Expression:
IsActive == false
and not
(
Model.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,
"(?i)USERELATIONSHIP\s*\(\s*\'*" +
current.FromTable.Name + "\'*\[" + 
current.FromColumn.Name + "\]\s*,\s*\'*" +
current.ToTable.Name + "\'*\[" +
current.ToColumn.Name + "\]"))
or
Model.AllCalculationItems.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,
"(?i)USERELATIONSHIP\s*\(\s*\'*" +
current.FromTable.Name + "\'*\[" + 
current.FromColumn.Name + "\]\s*,\s*\'*" +
current.ToTable.Name + "\'*\[" +
current.ToColumn.Name + "\]"))
)

ID: [DAX Expressions] Avoid using '1-(x/y)' syntax
Name: AVOID_USING_'1-(X/Y)'_SYNTAX
Description:
Instead of using the '1-(x/y)' or '1+(x/y)' syntax to achieve a percentage calculation, use the basic DAX functions (as shown below). Using the improved syntax will generally improve the performance. The '1+/-...' syntax always returns a value whereas the solution without the '1+/-...' does not (as the value may be 'blank'). Therefore the '1+/-...' syntax may return more rows/columns which may result in a slower query speed.

Let's clarify with an example:

Avoid this: 1 - SUM ( 'Sales'[CostAmount] ) / SUM( 'Sales'[SalesAmount] )
Better: DIVIDE ( SUM ( 'Sales'[SalesAmount] ) - SUM ( 'Sales'[CostAmount] ), SUM ( 'Sales'[SalesAmount] ) )
Best: VAR x = SUM ( 'Sales'[SalesAmount] ) RETURN DIVIDE ( x - SUM ( 'Sales'[CostAmount] ), x )

ID: [DAX Expressions] The EVALUATEANDLOG function should not be used in production models
Name: EVALUATEANDLOG_SHOULD_NOT_BE_USED_IN_PRODUCTION_MODELS
Description:
The EVALUATEANDLOG function is meant to be used only in development/test environments and should not be used in production models.

Reference: https://pbidax.wordpress.com/2022/08/16/introduce-the-dax-evaluateandlog-function/

ID: [Error Prevention] Data columns must have a source column
Name: DATA_COLUMNS_MUST_HAVE_A_SOURCE_COLUMN
Description: Data columns must have a source column. A data column without a source column will cause an error when processing the model.

ID: [Error Prevention] Expression-reliant objects must have an expression
Name: EXPRESSION_RELIANT_OBJECTS_MUST_HAVE_AN_EXPRESSION
Description: Calculated columns, calculation items and measures must have an expression. Without an expression, these objects will not show any values.

ID: [Error Prevention] Avoid structured data sources with provider partitions
Name: AVOID_STRUCTURED_DATA_SOURCES_WITH_PROVIDER_PARTITIONS
Description:
Power BI does not support provider (a.k.a. 'legacy') partitions which reference structured data sources. Partitions which reference structured data sources must use the M-language. Otherwise, 'provider' partitions must reference a 'provider' data source. This can be resolved by converting the structured data source into a provider data source (see 2nd reference link below).

Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/admin/service-premium-connect-tools#data-source-declaration
Reference: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/convertdatasources

ID: [Error Prevention] Avoid the USERELATIONSHIP function and RLS against the same table
Name: AVOID_THE_USERELATIONSHIP_FUNCTION_AND_RLS_AGAINST_THE_SAME_TABLE
Description:
The USERELATIONSHIP function may not be used against a table which also leverages row-level security (RLS). This will generate an error when using the particular measure in a visual. This rule will highlight the table which is used in a measure's USERELATIONSHIP function as well as RLS.

Reference: https://blog.crossjoin.co.uk/2013/05/10/userelationship-and-tabular-row-security/

ID: [Error Prevention] Relationship columns should be of the same data type
Name: RELATIONSHIP_COLUMNS_SAME_DATA_TYPE
Description: Columns used in a relationship should be of the same data type. Ideally, they will be of integer data type (see the related rule '[Formatting] Relationship columns should be of integer data type'). Having columns within a relationship which are of different data types may lead to various issues.

ID: [Error Prevention] Avoid invalid characters in names
Name: AVOID_INVALID_NAME_CHARACTERS
Description: This rule identifies if a name for a given object in your model (i.e. table/column/measure) which contains an invalid character. Invalid characters will cause an error when deploying the model (and failure to deploy). This rule has a fix expression which converts the invalid character into a space, resolving the issue.
Scope: Table, Measure, Hierarchy, Level, Perspective, Partition, DataColumn, CalculatedColumn, CalculatedTable, CalculatedTableColumn, KPI, ModelRole, CalculationGroup, CalculationItem

ID: [Error Prevention] Avoid invalid characters in descriptions
Name: AVOID_INVALID_DESCRIPTION_CHARACTERS
Description: This rule identifies if a description for a given object in your model (i.e. table/column/measure) which contains an invalid character. Invalid characters will cause an error when deploying the model (and failure to deploy). This rule has a fix expression which converts the invalid character into a space, resolving the issue.
Scope: Table, Measure, Hierarchy, Level, Perspective, Partition, DataColumn, CalculatedColumn, CalculatedTable, CalculatedTableColumn, KPI, ModelRole, CalculationGroup, CalculationItem

ID: [Error Prevention] Set IsAvailableInMdx to true on necessary columns
Name: SET_ISAVAILABLEINMDX_TO_TRUE_ON_NECESSARY_COLUMNS
Description: In order to avoid errors, ensure that attribute hierarchies are enabled if a column is used for sorting another column, used in a hierarchy, used in variations, or is sorted by another column.
Expression:
IsAvailableInMDX = false

and
(
UsedInSortBy.Any()
or
UsedInHierarchies.Any()
or
UsedInVariations.Any()
or
SortByColumn != null
)

ID: [Maintenance] Remove unnecessary columns
Name: UNNECESSARY_COLUMNS
Description: Hidden columns that are not referenced by any DAX expressions, relationships, hierarchy levels or Sort By-properties should be removed.
Expression:
(IsHidden or Table.IsHidden)


and ReferencedBy.Count = 0


and (not UsedInRelationships.Any())


and (not UsedInSortBy.Any())


and (not UsedInHierarchies.Any())


and (not Table.RowLevelSecurity.Any(
it <> null and it.IndexOf("[" + current.Name + "]", "OrdinalIgnoreCase") >= 0
))

 and (not Model.Roles.Any(RowLevelSecurity.Any(
it <> null and 
(
it.IndexOf(current.Table.Name + "[" + current.Name + "]", "OrdinalIgnoreCase") >= 0 or
 it.IndexOf("'" + current.Table.Name + "'[" + current.Name + "]", "OrdinalIgnoreCase") >= 0
 )
)))
and not (
ObjectLevelSecurity.Any(it.ToString() == "None"))
and not (
Table.ObjectLevelSecurity.Any(it.ToString() == "None"))

ID: [Maintenance] Remove unnecessary measures
Name: UNNECESSARY_MEASURES
Description: Hidden measures that are not referenced by any DAX expressions should be removed for maintainability

ID: [Maintenance] Avoid local file connections in Power Query
Name: AVOID_LOCAL_FILE_PATHS
Description: A partition uses File.Contents(), which reads files from the local machine. Local file connections cannot be refreshed in the Power BI Service or by other team members — the file is not accessible outside the original machine. Move the file to a shared location (SharePoint, OneDrive) and update the connection accordingly.

ID: [Maintenance] Remove auto-generated Transform File queries from folder connectors
Name: AVOID_AUTO_GENERATED_TRANSFORM_FILE_QUERIES
Description: Power BI auto-generates helper queries ('Transform File') when combining files from a folder. These auto-generated steps add unnecessary complexity, are hard to maintain, and often contain redundant transformations. Refactor the folder combination logic manually using a custom function instead.

ID: [Maintenance] Fix referential integrity violations
Name: FIX_REFERENTIAL_INTEGRITY_VIOLATIONS
Description:
This rule highlights relationships which have referential integrity violations. This indicates that there are values in the table on the 'from' side of the relationship which do not exist in the table on the 'to' side of the relationship. Referential integrity violations will also produce the 'blank' member value in slicers. It is recommended to fix these issues by ensuring that the 'to' table's primary key column has all the values in the 'from' table's foreign key column.

Reference: https://blog.enterprisedna.co/vertipaq-analyzer-tutorial-relationships-referential-integrity/

ID: [Maintenance] Remove data sources not referenced by any partitions
Name: REMOVE_DATA_SOURCES_NOT_REFERENCED_BY_ANY_PARTITIONS
Description: Data sources which are not referenced by any partitions may be removed.

ID: [Maintenance] Remove roles with no members
Name: REMOVE_ROLES_WITH_NO_MEMBERS
Description: May remove roles with no members.

ID: [Maintenance] Ensure tables have relationships
Name: ENSURE_TABLES_HAVE_RELATIONSHIPS
Description: This rule highlights tables which are not connected to any other table in the model with a relationship.

ID: [Maintenance] Visible objects with no description
Name: OBJECTS_WITH_NO_DESCRIPTION
Description:
Add descriptions to objects. These descriptions are shown on hover within the Field List in Power BI Desktop. Additionally, you can leverage these descriptions to create an automated data dictionary (see link below).
Reference: https://www.elegantbi.com/post/datadictionary
Scope: Table, Measure, DataColumn, CalculatedColumn, CalculatedTable, CalculatedTableColumn, CalculationGroup

ID: [Maintenance] Perspectives with no objects
Name: PERSPECTIVES_WITH_NO_OBJECTS
Description: Perspectives that contain no objects (tables) are most likely not necessary. In this rule, it is only necessary to check tables as adding a column/measure/hierarchy to a perspective also adds the table to the perspective. Additionally, tables in general covers calculated tables and calculation groups as well.

ID: [Maintenance] Calculation groups with no calculation items
Name: CALCULATION_GROUPS_WITH_NO_CALCULATION_ITEMS
Description: Calculation groups have no function unless they have calculation items.

ID: [Naming Conventions] Partition name should match table name for single partition tables
Name: PARTITION_NAME_SHOULD_MATCH_TABLE_NAME_FOR_SINGLE_PARTITION_TABLES
Description: Tables with just one partition should match their table and partition names.Tables with more than one partition should have each partition name starting with the table name.

ID: [Naming Conventions] Object names must not contain special characters
Name: SPECIAL_CHARS_IN_OBJECT_NAMES
Description: Tabs, line breaks, etc.
Scope: Model, Table, Measure, Hierarchy, Perspective, Partition, DataColumn, CalculatedColumn, CalculatedTable, CalculatedTableColumn, CalculationGroup, CalculationItem

ID: [Naming Conventions] Trim object names
Name: TRIM_OBJECT_NAMES
Description: Unintentionally leaving a trailing space in an object name is a common occurrence when copying/duplicating objects in Tabular Editor.
Scope: Model, Table, Measure, Hierarchy, Level, Perspective, Partition, ProviderDataSource, DataColumn, CalculatedColumn, CalculatedTable, CalculatedTableColumn, StructuredDataSource, NamedExpression, ModelRole, CalculationGroup, CalculationItem

ID: [Formatting] Format flag columns as Yes/No value strings
Name: FORMAT_FLAG_COLUMNS_AS_YES/NO_VALUE_STRINGS
Description: Flags must be properly formatted as Yes/No as this is easier to read than using 0/1 integer values.
Expression:
(
Name.StartsWith("Is") and 
DataType = "Int64" and 
not (IsHidden or Table.IsHidden)
) 
or

(
Name.EndsWith(" Flag") and 
DataType <> "String" and 
not (IsHidden or Table.IsHidden)
)

ID: [Formatting] Objects should not start or end with a space
Name: OBJECTS_SHOULD_NOT_START_OR_END_WITH_A_SPACE
Description: Objects should not start or end with a space
Scope: Model, Table, Measure, Hierarchy, Perspective, Partition, DataColumn, CalculatedColumn

ID: [Formatting] Provide format string for "Date" columns
Name: DATECOLUMN_FORMATSTRING
Description: Columns of type "DateTime" that have "Month" in their names should be formatted as "mm/dd/yyyy".

ID: [Formatting] Provide format string for "Month" columns
Name: MONTHCOLUMN_FORMATSTRING
Description: Columns of type "DateTime" that have "Month" in their names should be formatted as "MMMM yyyy".
Expression: Name.IndexOf("Month", "OrdinalIgnoreCase") >= 0 and DataType = "DateTime" and FormatString <> "MMMM yyyy"

ID: [Formatting] Provide format string for measures
Name: PROVIDE_FORMAT_STRING_FOR_MEASURES
Description: Visible measures should have their format string property assigned
Expression:
not IsHidden 
and not Table.IsHidden 
and string.IsNullOrWhitespace(FormatString)

ID: [Formatting] Do not summarize numeric columns
Name: NUMERIC_COLUMN_SUMMARIZE_BY
Description: Numeric columns (integer, decimal, double) should have their SummarizeBy property set to "None" to avoid accidental summation in Power BI (create measures instead).
Expression:
(
DataType = "Int64"
or 
DataType="Decimal" 
or 
DataType="Double"
)

and 
SummarizeBy <> "None"

and not (IsHidden or Table.IsHidden)

ID: [Formatting] Percentages should be formatted with thousands separators and 1 decimal
Name: PERCENTAGE_FORMATTING

ID: [Formatting] Whole numbers should be formatted with thousands separators and no decimals
Name: INTEGER_FORMATTING
Expression: not FormatString.Contains("$") and not FormatString.Contains("%") and not (FormatString = "#,0" or FormatString = "#,0.0")

ID: [Formatting] Relationship columns should be of integer data type
Name: RELATIONSHIP_COLUMNS_SHOULD_BE_OF_INTEGER_DATA_TYPE
Description: It is a best practice for relationship columns to be of integer data type. This applies not only to data warehousing but data modeling as well.

ID: [Formatting] Add data category for columns
Name: ADD_DATA_CATEGORY_FOR_COLUMNS
Description:
Add Data Category property for appropriate columns.

Reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/power-bi/transform-model/desktop-data-categorization
Expression:
string.IsNullOrWhitespace(DataCategory)
and
(
(
Name.ToLower().Contains("country")
or 

Name.ToLower().Contains("continent"
)
or
Name.ToLower().Contains("city")
)
and DataType == "String"
)
or 
(
(
Name.ToLower() == "latitude" 
 or 
Name.ToLower() == "longitude")
and (DataType == DataType.Decimal or DataType == DataType.Double)
)

ID: [Formatting] Hide foreign keys
Name: HIDE_FOREIGN_KEYS
Description: Foreign keys should always be hidden.
Expression:
UsedInRelationships.Any(FromColumn.Name == current.Name and FromCardinality == "Many")

and

IsHidden == false

ID: [Formatting] Mark primary keys
Name: MARK_PRIMARY_KEYS
Description: Set the 'Key' property to 'True' for primary key columns within the column properties.
Expression:
UsedInRelationships.Any(ToTable.Name == current.Table.Name and ToColumn.Name == current.Name and ToCardinality == "One")

and

IsKey == false
and
current.Table.DataCategory != "Time"

ID: [Formatting] Hide fact table columns
Name: HIDE_FACT_TABLE_COLUMNS
Description: It is a best practice to hide fact table columns that are used for aggregation in measures.
Expression:
(
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)COUNT\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))

or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)COUNTBLANK\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))

or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)SUM\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))
or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)AVERAGE\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))

or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)VALUES\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))

or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)DISTINCT\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))
or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)DISTINCTCOUNT\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))

or

ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)MIN\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))

or

ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)MAX\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))

or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)COUNTA\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))


or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)AVERAGEA\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))

or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)MAXA\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))

or
ReferencedBy.AllMeasures.Any(RegEx.IsMatch(Expression,"(?i)MINA\s*\(\s*\'*" + outerit.Table.Name + "\'*\[" + outerit.Name + "\]\s*\)"))
)

and IsHidden == false

and (DataType == "Int64" || DataType == "Decimal" || DataType == "Double")

ID: [Formatting] First letter of objects must be capitalized
Name: FIRST_LETTER_OF_OBJECTS_MUST_BE_CAPITALIZED
Scope: Table, Measure, Hierarchy, CalculatedColumn, CalculatedTable, CalculatedTableColumn, CalculationGroup

ID: [Formatting] Month (as a string) must be sorted
Name: MONTH_(AS_A_STRING)_MUST_BE_SORTED
Description: This rule highlights month columns which are strings and are not sorted. If left unsorted, they will sort alphabetically (i.e. April, August...). Make sure to sort such columns so that they sort properly (January, February, March...).
Expression:
Name.ToUpper().Contains("MONTH")
and
! Name.ToUpper().Contains("MONTHS") 
and 


DataType == DataType.String 
and 
SortByColumn == null
